_doc: Golden-Scenario Suite fixtures for CANCEL / REFUND (ADR 0009, issue #206).
PRD #155 makes it a hard rule that a changed money rule must be pinned here.
#172's compensating cash-out — the single most consequential money change in
that PRD — had NO cross-implementation contract at all until this file, which
is exactly what #206 was filed to fix. Each scenario is a checkout (asserted
by the usual `expected` block) FOLLOWED BY a cancel (asserted by the `cancel`
block), so every reversal is measured against a sale whose own rows are
already pinned.
THE RULE, as migration 0170's header states it: a cancel APPENDS one
compensating row per reversible original, dated on the cancel day, and
mutates nothing. Row count after a cancel = originals + one per reversible
original. Concretely:
* every ORIGINAL payment row survives, UNVOIDED, at its original amount —
a sale day the owner already reviewed and banked against never shrinks
behind them (#172). This is the OPPOSITE of the pre-#155 rule, which
voided each original in place AND posted a full-amount refund for it.
* `sale`          -> a POSITIVE `refund` for the same amount;
* `crate_deposit` -> a NEGATIVE `crate_deposit` (#190/#201): in-family,
NEVER a `refund`. The collection was never in Cash sales, so its release
must not land in Cash refunds;
* `wallet_topup`  -> a NEGATIVE `wallet_topup`, so Debts collected nets to
zero;
* every wallet leg the sale posted is reversed by an APPENDED opposite leg
(goods debit -> `refund` credit, payment credit -> `void` debit, a held
`crate_deposit` credit -> a deposit-family `crate_deposit_refunded`
debit, #162), so the customer returns to their exact pre-sale balance;
* the shelf and the FIFO queue come back together: inventory is restored
and ONE FRESH cost layer is appended per line at the per-unit COGS the
sale snapshotted (#170 #7c). The seeded batch stays drawn down — topping
it back up as well would double-restore (#187 / migration 0167).
ONE HALF OF THE RULE IS NOT IN THIS FILE, because a fixture cannot express
it: "the reversal lands on the CANCEL day" only means anything because the
ORIGINAL keeps its own `created_at`, and a golden run happens in a single
instant, so the two dates cannot be compared to each other. Each runner
therefore snapshots every original payment row's full state (type, method,
amount, created_at, voided_at) BEFORE the cancel and reports any that
changed or vanished as `CancelOutcome.mutatedOriginals`, which
`expectGoldenCancel` requires to be empty. The day-boundary case itself is
pinned separately, with a backdated sale, in test/orders/cancel_cashout_test.
ARM COVERAGE — every scenario here is `dart_arm_only: true` TODAY, and that
is a statement about the cloud, not about the rule. The SQL twin
(`pos_cancel_order`) implements exactly these expectations as of #201 /
supabase/migrations/0170_flag_gated_rpc_money_parity.sql, but 0170 is NOT
DEPLOYED: the RPC arm runs against live Supabase, where the shipped function
still voids originals in place, so it would fail every scenario in this file.
Drop the flag once 0170 is deployed — and note that the RPC runner must FIRST
grow a cancel step (call `pos_cancel_order`, collect the post-cancel rows,
call `expectGoldenCancel`). It has none today, so un-flagging alone would
assert only the checkout half; `checkout_order_golden_test` fails loudly on a
cancel scenario for that reason rather than passing silently.
The CRATE-track leg is deliberately NOT modelled here. A cancel of a
crate-track (non-money) sale reverses the customer's issued crate debt via
the Crate Pool seam (#162), but 0170's `pos_cancel_order` writes no crate
rows at all (ADR 0020 makes the seam the sole crate-table writer, and the
server has no crate arm) — a fixture no second implementation can ever
satisfy is not a contract. That rule stays pinned on the Dart arm in
test/crates/crate_cancel_completes_ledger_test.dart.

scenarios.name: cancel (#172): the paid sale row survives untouched and a dated refund is appended
scenarios._note: Dart-arm only until migration 0170 is deployed — see ARM COVERAGE above. A walk-in ₦2,000 cash sale, then cancelled: 2 payment rows (the original + its reversal), never 1 mutated one.

scenarios.name: cancel (#190/#201): a held crate deposit is released in-family, as a NEGATIVE crate_deposit
scenarios._note: Dart-arm only until migration 0170 is deployed — see ARM COVERAGE above. A money-track deposit sale (₦3,000 goods + ₦1,500 deposit = ₦4,500 tendered), then cancelled. The goods `sale` row refunds AS-IS (the #175 split already excluded the deposit, so subtracting it again would double-count), and the deposit is released as a NEGATIVE `crate_deposit` — not a second cash-out — so the held-deposit line nets to zero while Cash refunds moves only by the goods.

scenarios.name: cancel (#201): an overpayment's wallet_topup is reversed in-family, as a NEGATIVE wallet_topup
scenarios._note: Dart-arm only until migration 0170 is deployed — see ARM COVERAGE above. A ₦3,000 sale tendered ₦3,500: the ₦500 excess is the customer's credit, booked as a `wallet_topup` (#175), never as a sale. Cancelling reverses it inside its own family so Debts collected nets to zero, and the customer's balance returns to its pre-sale ₦0 rather than keeping a windfall.
